name: Mailcoach Cloud
tagline: Hosted newsletters, campaigns, automations, transactional mail, and analytics

pricing.notes: The pricing model is not safely comparable as one fixed monthly USD amount. Review the official source before publication.

tiers.name: Cloud
tiers.limits: 2,000 emails included, unlimited contacts, unlimited lists, unlimited automations.
tiers.notes: Published at €9.99/month excluding VAT; converted at about 1 EUR = 1.155 USD on 2026-08-10.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 14-day trial with 100 emails.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly only; usage-based monthly invoice; annual prepayment not available
pricing.hiddenCosts: Extra emails are usage-based but the numeric per-email fee did not render; VAT excluded; BYO provider can save 0.001/email; final invoice issued after cancellation.

verdictSummary: The visible email marketing loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Mailcoach Cloud earns its keep through deliverability, reputation, network, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a small email marketing editor and subscriber database that exports clean HTML and sends only through a reputable user-supplied email provider.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: transactional or bulk email provider key in .env
whatYouLose: sender reputation, deliverability, and suppression handling
whyPeopleStillPay: Mailcoach Cloud: The editor is trivial compared with inbox placement, compliance, reputation, unsubscribe handling, analytics, and audience growth infrastructure.
ongoingBurden: Own consent records, suppression lists, bounces, complaints, DNS, templates, accessibility, segmentation, and privacy requests.

priorArt.name: listmonk
priorArt.desc: High-performance self-hosted newsletter and mailing-list manager.

alternatives.name: Brevo Free
alternatives.desc: Campaigns, transactional mail and automation with a strict daily send valve.

facts.dataFormat: Contacts, campaigns, consent records, and message events live in Brevo's cloud; contacts can be exported as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: Brevo Free replaces low-volume campaigns and transactional sends, but its 300-message daily cap and thinner free automation/reporting make it a much smaller service than Mailcoach Cloud.
facts.setupBlocker: Authenticating a custom sending domain requires adding DNS records.

alternatives.name: Loops Free
alternatives.desc: Hosted lifecycle and transactional email with every feature for 1,000 contacts.

facts.dataFormat: Contacts, custom properties, events, workflows, and message history live in Loops' cloud; contacts can be imported/exported as CSV.
facts.gapVsPaid: Loops Free is startup-focused and easy to operate, but 1,000 contacts and 4,000 emails per 30 days leave far less room than Mailcoach Cloud's usage-based campaign and transactional workload.
facts.setupBlocker: You must authenticate a sending domain and instrument your app or API before lifecycle emails become useful.

alternatives.name: Mautic
alternatives.desc: Campaigns, automations, transactional sends and analytics without contact pricing; the stack is anything but lightweight.

alternatives.name: Notifuse
alternatives.desc: Campaigns, transactional mail, visual automations and analytics in one current self-hosted product.

facts.install: Notifuse Cloud signup or self-host with Docker
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted contact, campaign, event, and analytics data lives in PostgreSQL; uploaded assets use S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Notifuse has the right campaign-plus-transactional shape, but the self-hosted route makes you operate PostgreSQL, storage, and a separate delivery provider instead of buying a managed service.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs Docker, PostgreSQL, object storage, a public domain, and a separately configured SMTP or email API provider.

alternatives.name: Plunk
alternatives.desc: The same campaign-plus-transactional shape with workflow automation; Docker is the subscription.

facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted data lives in PostgreSQL, queues in Redis, and uploads in bundled MinIO or another S3-compatible store.
facts.gapVsPaid: Plunk combines campaigns, transactional email, and workflows, but its self-hosted stack and mandatory external sender are substantially less turnkey than Mailcoach Cloud.
facts.setupBlocker: The self-host path needs Docker, several subdomains, DNS/TLS, and an AWS SES account with credentials and domain verification.

alternatives.name: Sender Free
alternatives.desc: Hosted campaigns, transactional sends and workflows in one free account; advanced reporting is lighter.

facts.dataFormat: Subscribers, campaigns, automations, and engagement events live in Sender's cloud; subscriber data can be exported.
facts.gapVsPaid: Sender Free is useful for small hosted campaigns and workflows, but its subscriber/send limits, single-user free account, and vendor branding are materially tighter than Mailcoach Cloud.
facts.setupBlocker: A custom sending domain must be verified with DNS records for reliable delivery.

rejectedAlternatives.name: listmonk
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Campaigns and transactional API are excellent; the missing automation builder leaves a core job uncovered.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Mailcoach Cloud is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Mailcoach Cloud, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL.
Primary job: Build a small email marketing editor and subscriber database that exports clean HTML and sends only through a reputable user-supplied email provider.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: payments, recommendations, and audience network; sender reputation, deliverability, and suppression handling; sender reputation and deliverability operations.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
